decision: What did we find? The reviewed fixed scientific matrix found that both observers accepted twelve independently audited inputs (24 scientific checks), and all twelve empty-input baselines completed. No configured limit or process-control fault affected the fixed scientific matrix; the earlier construction failures, including a sandbox monitoring denial, remain preserved. All eighteen Nanoda runs have zero RSS sample points; the supervisor was configured with a 10 ms target cadence, but the records do not establish achieved cadence or prove why no sample was captured. Their sampled group RSS remains unknown, while the reviewed receipts preserve separate wait4 child-accounting high-water values. Repository completion requires successful file-backed full-suite and ordered closure receipts; closure attempt 0001 failed during the temporary state-edit race; attempt 0002 preserved a missing literal READY-count status gate after host preflight and input inventory. Attempt 0003 passed preflight gates but the full suite found portable replay did not yet cover newly committed closure-control supervisor receipts. Its full log is preserved; these repository validation failures do not change the scientific result. Is it interesting? Yes, as a finite valid-input and measurement package that exposes a short-process observation gap; it found no checker defect and establishes no general performance or correctness claim. Does it require more work? Retain all local assets and take no upstream action. Select RESOURCE-SHORT-PROCESS-MEMORY-AUDIT-1 READY and unstarted to audit exactly those eighteen receipts, wait4 attribution and the Darwin identity limits, then define a future reporting/metadata rule.

categories.assessment: The fixed resource matrix is complete with 24 ACCEPTED checks and 12 successful baselines; all 18 Nanoda records have zero RSS samples despite the supervisor's configured 10 ms target cadence. The result does not establish the achieved sampling cadence or why no sample was captured. The source-site/configuration boundary still blocks BUILD-MODE, whose previous source scan found no realistic input-driven overflow trigger.

The twelve generated/audited inputs, 36 fresh-process observations, preserved construction failures, and portable receipt replay are reusable. A precise distinction remains between sampled process-group RSS (null for Nanoda) and its wait4 child-accounting high-water. The supervisor had a configured 10 ms target cadence; achieved cadence and the reason no sample was captured are not established. Historical runtime metadata omits the full kernel build string.

The matrix found no checker mismatch, configured resource limit, or scientific control fault. The owner’s hold on Kiota/Nanoda follow-up remains; no upstream issue, PR, or contact is supported by this evidence.

Reuse the existing wait4 supervisor, all 18 frozen Nanoda receipts, the prior XNU-main attribution correction, Apple wait4(2) documentation, and pinned Python 3.10 os.wait4 documentation. Apple documents returned resource usage for the terminated process and its children; this does not turn the value into a simultaneous group peak. Exact historical XNU correspondence remains limited because runtime_platform binds Darwin 24.6.0/arm64 but no full kernel build string.

A read-only 18-row receipt/source audit is immediately feasible and requires no checker execution, input mutation, or new measurement claim. It can clarify current evidence and establish a future exact-kernel metadata rule. BUILD-MODE lacks a viable site; Arena theorem companion lacks its asymmetric refusal preflight; CVC-4 depends on CVC-3 SUCCESS although CVC-3 closed BOUNDED_UNRESOLVED; transfer waits for owner-provided independent input/custodian.
